note: DSE Toolkit tools for the HQ Tools page. The runner only runs these; it never sends, posts or pays.

dse.daily.label: My engine: next send lists
dse.daily.help: Builds the engine's next dated send lists: finds new leads (or checks your seed websites), checks what each one is missing, drops anyone already on your lists, picks each lead's channel within your daily caps, and drafts the opener in your wording. They appear in the Send Desk.

fields.name: per_day
fields.label: Leads per day (empty = the engine's setting)

dse.list.label: Leads + problem check (the daily one)
dse.list.help: Finds independent businesses of one type near your cities, keeps those with a live website, checks what each site is missing for your path, and writes a ready opener per lead. Run 'Download business data' for that type once first. Spot-check, then Add to my CRM.

fields.name: pack

fields.name: kind

fields.hint: Any business you sell to: dentists, wedding photographers, dog trainers. Types we already know are used as they are; a new one is matched to Foursquare's business categories and remembered. The first time for a new type it builds its data (a few minutes).

fields.name: skip

dse.podcasts.label: Podcast leads (Broadcast Engine)
dse.podcasts.help: Active business podcasts from Apple Podcasts' free search, with what each show is missing (gaps between episodes, no video, thin show notes) and the host's public email when the feed lists it.

fields.name: genre
fields.label: Genre
fields.hint: Pick one or type any topic. A genre of your own searches Apple Podcasts by your topics above.

dse.check.label: Problem check on a list
dse.check.help: Checks every website in one of your lists for what your path sells, adds the gaps and an opener per row.

fields.name: pack
fields.label: Your path or your own check

dse.check_one.label: Problem check on one website
dse.check_one.help: One website, results in the log. Good for a parish you know, a shop from the Meta Ad Library, or a lead someone referred.

fields.name: pack
fields.label: Your path or your own check

dse.find.label: Leads only (no check)
dse.find.help: Just the lead list: independent businesses of one type with a live website.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Business type (type any business, or pick from the list)
fields.hint: Any business you sell to: dentists, wedding photographers, dog trainers. Types we already know are used as they are; a new one is matched to Foursquare's business categories and remembered. The first time for a new type it builds its data (a few minutes).

fields.name: words
fields.label: Words the business's website must use (optional, your own; separate with commas)

fields.name: skip
fields.label: Leave out businesses whose name has these words (optional, your own)

dse.mystery_new.label: CareBridge: start a mystery-shop tracker
dse.mystery_new.help: Turns a home-care lead list into a tracker. You send each enquiry yourself, then fill in when you sent it and when they replied.

dse.mystery_score.label: CareBridge: score agencies by reply time
dse.mystery_score.help: Hot = no reply after 48 h or a reply after 24 h+; Warm = 1-24 h; Cold = within the hour. Reach out to Hot and Warm only.

dse.build.label: Download business data (once per type)
dse.build.help: Downloads one or more business types from Foursquare's free open data (needs your free Hugging Face token set on the PC; README). Do it once, then monthly.

howto.ask.label: How to do it (your path's tools)
howto.ask.help: Step-by-step recipes written from the tools' official help pages: Clay, Apollo, HubSpot, Sales Navigator, Instantly, Lemlist, n8n, Vapi, Cal.com, GoHighLevel, Klaviyo, Descript, CapCut, LinkedIn posts, sales calls and the whole GTM system. Each recipe gives the goal, what to have ready, steps with why each matters and what you should see, mistakes to avoid, a 'you are done when' check, the official source links and the date it was checked. Ask in your own words, like: enrich my list with emails in clay. Menus and plans change: if a button differs, open the source link in the answer.

fields.name: question
fields.label: What do you want to do?

chat.ask.label: HQ chat: ask anything
chat.ask.help: Ask anything about selling, discovery calls, objections, cold messages, follow-ups, pricing and proposals, freelancing, international clients, planning, focus, decisions, rejection, writing, or any tool in the stack. Answers are grounded in HQ's researched guides and recipes. Three levels, best available is used: (1) Claude, the strongest: set your own Claude API key as the Windows user variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, run pip install anthropic, and restart the runner (your question and the matching guide text go to Anthropic, you pay your own usage; nothing else is sent unless you ask about your progress). (2) Free local AI with Ollama: install it from ollama.com, run ollama pull gemma3:4b (about 3.3 GB, needs about 8 GB RAM, also reads pictures), set OLLAMA_MODEL=gemma3:4b and restart the runner. gemma3:1b works on small PCs but gives thinner answers. (3) With neither, you get the matching researched guide or recipe in full. The answer says which one wrote it. To ask about a picture in Citadel, use DBI-AI with an image-capable model. Mentors: ask for a quote, a mentor, or name someone (what did Seneca say about anger?) and real passages from the Voices library, with their sources, are shown beside the answer. Matching is by words, not by meaning, so they are never added to an ordinary answer unasked.

fields.name: question
fields.label: Your question (up to 2000 characters)
fields.placeholder: a client says it is too expensive

fields.name: model
fields.label: Model (optional: auto, library, claude or ollama:NAME)

fields.name: mentors
fields.label: Mentor passages from the Voices library

choices.label: Auto: only when I ask for a mentor, a quote or name someone

app.build.label: App Builder: build any website or app
app.build.help: Builds a real, working project for you: a website, web app (installs on phones), native phone app (iPhone + Android), desktop app (Windows/Mac) or TV app (Samsung, LG, Android TV). Pick a starting point (landing page, dashboard, store, booking), your name, colour and one line about it. You get a folder in builds/ with the app, a README with the exact commands to run and publish it, a BUILD-BRIEF of what to build next, and rules so an AI coding agent can carry on. Needs Node.js LTS (nodejs.org) for everything except the plain website. Tick 'Install and test the build' to have it prove the app builds (a few minutes). Nothing is published or paid for: you deploy yourself.

choices.label: Web app (installs on phones, works offline)
Landing page: home, pricing, about, contact

fields.name: brief
fields.label: One line: what it does and who it is for
fields.placeholder: Helps small recruiting agencies track every candidate

fields.name: email
fields.label: Contact email for forms (website only, optional)

fields.name: ai
fields.label: Let my free local AI (Ollama) write the headline and benefits

fields.name: install
fields.label: Install and test the build (a few minutes, needs Node.js)

yt.plan.label: YouTube Launchpad: plan my channel
yt.plan.help: Builds your whole YouTube channel plan from zero: your niche and promise, channel name ideas, setup checklist, the exact Partner Program (monetisation) numbers and what they mean in views, a faceless-safe policy guide, tools that cost nothing, a 13-week roadmap matched to your weekly hours, a weekly routine, and 30 video ideas with titles, hooks, thumbnail briefs and Shorts. Works faceless or on camera. Read CHANNEL-PLAN.md first. It teaches the method and the honest odds: it cannot promise income.

choices.label: AI tools and automation for work
Build websites and apps without code
Marketing for local and small businesses
Freelancing and selling your skills online
Podcasting and growing as a creator
Yes: I will be on camera
Earn from YouTube ads (the Partner Program) as the main income
Use the channel to bring clients to a service I sell (the most reliable route for new creators)
Earn from affiliate links and sponsors, with ads as a bonus
Build authority and a following first, income later

fields.name: hours
fields.label: Hours per week you can give

fields.name: name
fields.label: Channel name (optional: otherwise ideas are given)

yt.ideas.label: YouTube Launchpad: more video ideas
yt.ideas.help: Adds more video ideas to your channel's ideas.csv: titles that fit one window, a hook, a thumbnail brief and a Short for each. Give an angle (something you know well) and it puts a video on that first.

yt.script.label: YouTube Launchpad: write a video script
yt.script.help: Turns a video idea into a ready-to-record script plan: hook options, promise, sections with timing, on-screen cues, call to action, five title options, the thumbnail brief, description and pinned comment, a Short cut-down and a pre-upload checklist. Tick the AI box for a first draft from your own free Ollama (rewrite it in your voice: original content is what YouTube rewards).

fields.name: ai
fields.label: Add an AI first draft (needs Ollama, takes a few minutes)

yt.track.label: YouTube Launchpad: weekly numbers and progress
yt.track.help: Type this week's numbers from YouTube Studio (subscribers, watch hours in the last 12 months, Shorts views in the last 90 days, and if you can the click-through rate and average percentage viewed). It shows how far you are from the Partner Program numbers, your weekly pace, and the three things to fix next. Do it once a week.

yt.check.label: YouTube Launchpad: check a title and thumbnail
yt.check.help: Checks a video's packaging before you publish: title length and keyword position, shouting and clickbait wording, thumbnail words, and the first lines of the description. Gives a score and exact fixes.

dse.followups.label: My engine: plan follow-ups
dse.followups.help: Finds everyone you messaged (and marked Sent) who has not answered, works out who is due for a second or third message, drafts it and saves it as a list in the Send Desk. Rules: touch 2 and 3 come due 3 and 7 days after an email or Instagram message (Facebook 4 and 9, website form 5 and 12), Sundays are skipped, there is never a second Instagram DM (a comment, then a note by email or form), and it stops when they reply, book, are lost or you skip. Only rows you marked Sent count; it lists any you never marked. You still send every message yourself.

dse.outcomes.label: My engine: results
dse.outcomes.help: What the engine is really producing, from the taps you made in the Send Desk: messages sent, replies, calls booked, clients won and the monthly value, by channel, by the gap you led with, by wording and by touch. It only calls a difference when both sides have 30 or more sends in the same channel, and it tells you which first messages were never marked Sent or Skipped.

dse.import_check.label: My engine: check my file
dse.import_check.help: Go-to-Market and Authority engines build their lists from a file YOU make. Go-to-Market: a CSV exported from your own Clay, Apollo or HubSpot account, saved in engines/<engine>/imports/ on your PC. Authority: a CSV of experts you looked at and pasted by hand (name, profile_url, headline, connections, post_dates, post_1, post_2), saved in engines/<engine>/pasted/. This shows which columns were understood, how many rows, and the best prospects, so a wrong column shows up before you build a list. Nothing is scraped from LinkedIn or anywhere else.

ascent.callscore.label: The Ascent: score a sales call
ascent.callscore.help: After every sales call, real or a mock you recorded, rate it honestly in eight areas (0 missed, 1 partly, 2 done well). You get your score, the two weakest areas with a 10-minute drill each, and your numbers over time: show rate, close rate, cash per call, what you earned in commission, and your score trend. Be harsh: a scorecard that flatters you teaches nothing. Based on the up-front contract, SPIN-style questions and the pause-ask-answer objection routine (HQ recipe: Prepare and run a high-ticket sales call).

fields.name: talk
fields.label: How much of the call did YOU talk (%)

fields.name: a4
fields.label: 4. Cost of the problem (money or time)

fields.name: a8
fields.label: 8. Asked for the decision and followed up

dse.calls.label: The Ascent: my call history
dse.calls.help: Your logged calls and totals: how many, how many sold, cash, and your average score.

ascent.vet.label: The Ascent: vet a commission offer
ascent.vet.help: Before you give a high-ticket, commission-only offer your time, answer the questions (Yes, No or Not asked yet). You get a verdict (Walk away, Red, Amber, Unchecked, OK or Promising), the exact reasons, a ready message with the questions to put to them in writing, what to get in the contract, and what one sale and a target month would really need from you. Based on the FTC's job-scam advice (never pay for a job, earnings promises, fake checks, unverifiable employers) and practitioner guidance for commission contracts. It informs your decision; it is not legal advice. It saves the offer to your tracker.

fields.name: ticket
fields.label: Price of the offer they sell ($)

fields.name: target
fields.label: Monthly income you want from it ($)

fields.name: d_pay
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they ask you to pay anything to start: training, certification, starter kit, deposit, leads or software?

fields.name: d_contract
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they refuse to put the commission terms in writing before you start?

fields.name: d_earnings
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Did they promise or hint at what you will earn to get you to join (for example 'our closers make $20k a month', guaranteed income)?

fields.name: d_money
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Do they ask you to receive money, cash a check, forward payments, or buy gift cards?

fields.name: d_hidden
fields.label: DEALBREAKER: Is the company impossible to verify: no named owner, no registered business, or a website or contact that does not work?

fields.name: s_rate
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the commission rate, or what it is calculated on (cash collected or contract value), unclear?

fields.name: s_payout
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the payout later than 30 days after the client pays, or is no payout date stated?

fields.name: s_clawback
fields.label: SERIOUS: Can they take your commission back (refunds, chargebacks) with no written time window or cap?

fields.name: s_proof
fields.label: SERIOUS: Can you not verify real customers or results (no named customers, no reviews outside their own pages)?

fields.name: s_regulated
fields.label: SERIOUS: Is the offer in a regulated area (credit repair, lending, trading, investing, insurance) where selling may need a licence?

fields.name: s_leads
fields.label: SERIOUS: Will you be cold-calling your own leads, with no stated source or number of booked calls?

fields.name: s_exclusive
fields.label: SERIOUS: Do they want exclusivity or a non-compete without a guaranteed base or minimum?

fields.name: s_control
fields.label: SERIOUS: Are you called a contractor but told your hours, must follow a script you cannot change, and cannot work for others?

fields.name: s_nobody
fields.label: SERIOUS: Do they refuse to let you speak to a current closer or the person you would report to?

fields.name: c_payment
fields.label: CAUTION: Is there no clear way to be paid internationally (for example Wise, Payoneer or bank transfer), or unclear who pays the fees?

fields.name: c_pressure
fields.label: CAUTION: Do they pressure you to decide fast ('spots are filling', 'offer ends today')?

fields.name: c_recordings
fields.label: CAUTION: Are your calls recorded without being told how the recordings are used or who owns them?

fields.name: c_nda
fields.label: CAUTION: Is the NDA or ownership clause broader than the job (for example it stops you working in the industry afterwards)?

fields.name: c_refund_rate
fields.label: CAUTION: Do they refuse to say their refund or chargeback rate?

fields.name: p_contract
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Did they send a written agreement draft showing rate, base, payout date and clawback terms?

fields.name: p_named
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Can you name the founder and find the company in a business registry (US state registry or UK Companies House)?

fields.name: p_closer
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Did you speak to a current closer who confirmed pay and lead flow?

fields.name: p_inbound
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Do they supply warm leads (calls booked from their own content or ads)?

fields.name: p_reviews
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Do independent customers or reviews outside their own pages confirm the product works?

fields.name: p_data
fields.label: GOOD SIGN: Will you see your own call data and results (CRM or recordings) so you can prove your numbers?

dse.offers.label: The Ascent: my offer tracker
dse.offers.help: Every offer you vetted, best verdict first, with its status, price and commission.

dev.config.label: Dev: what is allowed on this PC
dev.config.help: Shows what the dev tools may do here (editing, tasks, pushing to GitHub, PowerShell). These switches can only be changed at the PC itself, never from here.

dev.workspaces.label: Dev: my workspaces
dev.workspaces.help: Lists your workspaces (project folders on this PC), what kind of project each is and which git branch it is on.

dev.new.label: Dev: start a new project
dev.new.help: Creates a project folder with starter code, a test and git, in one of 14 starters: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python (command line or web API), Java, Kotlin, C#, C, C++, Dart, Flutter, Go, Rust, PowerShell. Tick the last box to use the language's own generator when it is installed.

fields.name: official
fields.label: Use the language's own generator if installed

dev.clone.label: Dev: copy a GitHub repository here
dev.clone.help: Copies a repository from GitHub into a workspace so you can read and change it. Public repositories need no login; private ones use the GitHub login on this PC.

dev.repo.label: Dev: look at a GitHub repository
dev.repo.help: Reads a repository's description, language, stars and default branch from GitHub.

dev.issues.label: Dev: open issues of a GitHub repository
dev.issues.help: Lists the latest open issues and pull requests.

dev.tree.label: Dev: show the files
dev.tree.help: Lists the files and folders of a workspace.

dev.read.label: Dev: read a file
dev.read.help: Shows a file with line numbers. Files that hold secrets (.env, keys) are never shown.

fields.name: path
fields.label: File path inside the workspace (like src/app.py)

dev.search.label: Dev: search the code
dev.search.help: Finds lines matching a word or pattern in every file of the workspace.

dev.replace.label: Dev: change a line of code
dev.replace.help: Replaces text in a file. The old text must match exactly once. For bigger changes use Dev: let the AI make a change.

fields.name: path
fields.label: File path inside the workspace (like src/app.py)

dev.run.label: Dev: install, build, test or lint
dev.run.help: Runs the project's own install, build, test or lint step (npm, pip, Maven, Gradle, dotnet, CMake, Dart, Flutter, Cargo, Go). If a tool is missing it tells you the one command that installs it.

dev.status.label: Dev: what changed (git status)
dev.status.help: Shows the branch and which files changed.

dev.diff.label: Dev: show the changes (git diff)
dev.diff.help: Shows exactly what changed since the last commit.

dev.branch.label: Dev: start a branch
dev.branch.help: Creates and switches to a new git branch.

dev.commit.label: Dev: save a commit
dev.commit.help: Saves the current changes as a commit. Refuses if a file that looks like a secret would be included.

dev.pull.label: Dev: update from GitHub (pull)
dev.pull.help: Brings in new commits from GitHub (fast-forward only, it can never rewrite your work).

dev.push.label: Dev: push to GitHub
dev.push.help: Pushes the current branch to GitHub. Works only when you switched pushing on at this PC and the repository belongs to an account you allowed. From main it pushes a new dev/ branch instead; it never forces.

dev.pr.label: Dev: open a pull request
dev.pr.help: Opens a pull request on GitHub for the current branch (same permission as pushing, and your GitHub login on this PC).

dev.agent.label: Dev: let the AI make a change
dev.agent.help: An AI engineer reads the project, edits the files, runs the tests and saves the result on a NEW branch (dev/agent-...). It cannot leave the workspace, read secrets, run a shell or push. You read the diff, then push yourself. Uses Claude when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set on this PC, otherwise your local Ollama model.

fields.name: instruction
fields.label: What should change? (one or two sentences)

dev.shell.label: Dev: run a PowerShell command
dev.shell.help: Runs one PowerShell command inside a workspace. OFF unless you turned it on at this PC (allow_shell). Dangerous commands are refused, but this is not a sandbox: switch it on only if you accept that.

dse.cash.label: Cash Desk: am I on track this month?
dse.cash.help: Money you logged as received against your monthly target, the pace to the end of the month, the steps (messages, replies, calls, sales) from your own logs, and what it would take to close the gap using your own rates. Every figure comes from files on this PC and the report says so when there is too little data to trust a rate.

fields.name: target
fields.label: Monthly income target ($, empty = keep the saved one)

dse.cash_all.label: Cash Desk: all engines together
dse.cash_all.help: The same report for every engine added up, with the targets added up too.

dse.cashin.label: Cash Desk: log money I received
dse.cashin.help: Writes one line to the engine's cash file: the day, the amount, what kind of money it was and a short note. Log only money that has actually arrived (a refund is logged as a refund, not as a minus). Then shows the updated report.

dse.cashlog.label: Cash Desk: money I logged
dse.cashlog.help: Every payment logged for the engine, with the total.

dse.review.label: Weekly Review: what to do first this week
dse.review.help: Reads your send log, lists, follow-ups, calls, money and offers, and gives the 3 to 5 moves for the week in a fixed order, closest to money first. Each move says the exact step and which file the number came from. It sends and changes nothing.

dse.review_all.label: Weekly Review: all engines together
dse.review_all.help: The same review across every engine, moves ranked together.

dse.goal.label: Monthly goal: suggest, set or accept
dse.goal.help: Suggests next month's income goal from the money you logged in your last 3 complete months (plus a stretch you choose), shows the working, and says what each week would need using your own rates. Nothing changes unless you tick Accept the suggestion or type a goal yourself. A month with no goal of its own carries your standing target.

fields.name: month
fields.label: Month (YYYY-MM, empty = the next one to plan)

fields.name: apply
fields.label: Accept the suggestion as that month's goal

fields.name: set_to
fields.label: Or set the goal yourself ($, empty = leave it)

dse.enrich.label: Lead enrichment: find emails, owners and phones
dse.enrich.help: Takes a list of companies (a CSV with a website or domain column, like a Clay, Apollo or HubSpot export) and reads each company's own public website, politely, for emails, the owner's name, phone, contact form, booking tool, socials and what it is built with. Every finding names the page it came from. It scores each lead from rules you can read and keeps every column you gave it. Free: no paid service is used unless you pick a provider with your own key. The key is set on your PC, never here.

fields.name: icp
fields.label: Words you want to find on their site (optional, comma separated)

fields.name: engine
fields.label: Also save an import-ready copy in this engine (optional)

fields.name: max
fields.label: Most leads to look at in this run

fields.name: fast
fields.label: Fast (skip the hidden browser: quicker, misses sites drawn by JavaScript)

fields.name: provider
fields.label: Paid provider with YOUR own key (optional, empty = free only)

fields.name: budget
fields.label: Most paid lookups (only with a provider)

dse.enrich_site.label: Lead enrichment: look at one website
dse.enrich_site.help: Reads one company website and shows what a lead list would get: emails, owner, phone, form, booking tool, score and why. Nothing is saved.

dse.enrich_providers.label: Lead enrichment: which paid providers are set up
dse.enrich_providers.help: Lists the optional paid providers on this PC and whether their key is present (the key is never shown). To add one, run at your PC: python dse.py enrich --add-provider hunter, then set your own key in a Windows user variable.

dse.reply.label: Reply Desk: what kind of reply, and what to say
dse.reply.help: Paste a reply you received (line breaks become spaces). It says what kind it is (interested, question, price objection, already has someone, not now, not interested, wrong person, points to someone else, asks to stop, out of office, or unclear), shows the words that decided it, drafts a short honest answer in your name with [brackets] for facts only you know, and works out the day to follow up. Tick Record it, with the list name and row number, to put it in your send log (follow-ups stop) and to put unsubscribes and 'no thanks' on your do-not-contact list. It never sends anything.

fields.name: source
fields.label: List it answers (for example 2026-11-09), only to record it

fields.name: row
fields.label: Row number on that list, only to record it

fields.name: email
fields.label: Their email (only for the do-not-contact list)

fields.name: log
fields.label: Record it (send log and do-not-contact list)

dse.dnc.label: Reply Desk: my do-not-contact list
dse.dnc.help: Everyone who asked you to stop or said no, with the date and why. Outreach Preflight checks every list against it. No tool removes an entry.

dse.preflight.label: Outreach Preflight: check a list before you send
dse.preflight.help: Checks a send list row by row before anything goes out. Blockers: on your do-not-contact list, a missing or invalid address, already contacted, an unfilled placeholder left in the message. Warnings: spam trigger words, ALL CAPS, too many links, a long message, role or free mailboxes, no easy way to say no, no sender name or postal address, more email than your own cap. Optionally also checks your sending domain (mail servers, SPF, DMARC, DKIM). Tick the last box to save a copy without the blocked rows (the original is never touched). Guidance, not legal advice. It sends nothing.

fields.name: domain
fields.label: Your sending domain (the part after the @), optional

fields.name: clean
fields.label: Also save a copy without the blocked rows

dse.preflight_domain.label: Outreach Preflight: check my sending domain
dse.preflight_domain.help: Looks up your domain's mail servers, SPF record, DMARC record and the common DKIM names, and says what to fix before you send cold email from it. Nothing is sent or changed.

fields.name: domain
fields.label: Your sending domain (the part after the @)

dse.proposal.label: Proposal Builder: a one-page proposal after a good call
dse.proposal.help: Turns what you heard on the call into a clear one-page proposal, a cover email and a follow-up, in your name. Everything comes from what you type: their problem in their own words, what you will do, your price and deliverables. If you give what the problem costs them each month, it shows the yearly cost and the payback as plain arithmetic (never a promise of results). Optionally shows three options with the middle one recommended. It saves a text file and a print-ready page (open it in a browser and save as PDF), and marks [brackets] for anything only you know. It never sends anything.

fields.name: problem
fields.label: Their problem, in their own words

fields.name: offer
fields.label: What you will do for them (one sentence)

fields.name: price
fields.label: Your price (a whole number; leave 0 if you use options)

fields.name: deliverables
fields.label: What they get, separated by semicolons (for example Booking page; Reminder emails)

fields.name: cost_month
fields.label: What the problem costs them each month (from the call, 0 if unknown)

fields.name: options
fields.label: Optional three-way choice: Basic:800:2 pages; Standard:1500:5 pages; Premium:2800:10 pages

fields.name: currency
fields.label: Currency
fields.hint: A 3-letter currency code: USD, GBP, EUR, NGN, CAD, AUD, ZAR, GHS, INR...

fields.name: excludes
fields.label: What is NOT included (optional, but it prevents surprises)

dse.client_won.label: Client Desk: this proposal was accepted
dse.client_won.help: Turns a saved proposal into a client: price, deposit, timeline and deliverables carry over. Writes the onboarding checklist with dates, a welcome message in your name, a short agreement outline (a starting point, not legal advice) and the deposit invoice as a print-ready page. Nothing is sent: you send the welcome message, the agreement and the invoice yourself.

dse.client_list.label: Client Desk: my clients
dse.client_list.help: Every client with status, price, paid, what is owed now and the next deliverable.

dse.client_show.label: Client Desk: one client in full
dse.client_show.help: Onboarding tasks, deliverables with dates (late ones marked), and every invoice with what is outstanding.

dse.client_done.label: Client Desk: tick off a deliverable or task
dse.client_done.help: Marks a deliverable or an onboarding task as done (type a few words of its name). When the last deliverable is done it tells you to issue the final invoice.

fields.name: item
fields.label: A few words of its name

dse.client_invoice.label: Client Desk: issue the final or an extra invoice
dse.client_invoice.help: The final invoice is the balance of the price and follows delivery. An extra invoice is for something added (an amount and what it is for). Print-ready page; you send it yourself.

fields.name: note
fields.label: What it is for (extra invoices only)

dse.client_paid.label: Client Desk: money received for an invoice
dse.client_paid.help: Records a payment against an invoice (leave the amount empty for what is left) and adds it to the Cash Desk, so what you received stays true without typing it twice.

fields.name: amount
fields.label: Amount received (empty = the whole outstanding amount)

dse.cut_add.label: Cut Desk: add a student's agreement
dse.cut_add.help: Sets up the percentage cut a student owes you: your percent, whether it is of their gross earnings or net of the platform's fees, the currency and how they pay you (Grey or Payoneer). Writes an agreement starter to have checked. Nothing is sent. The agreement text is a starting point, not legal advice.

fields.name: percent
fields.label: Your cut (% of their earnings, 1 to 60)

choices.label: Earnings after the platform's own fees

fields.name: currency
fields.label: Currency
fields.hint: A 3-letter currency code: USD, GBP, EUR, NGN, CAD, AUD, ZAR, GHS, INR...

fields.name: due_days
fields.label: Days to pay after the invoice

dse.cut_report.label: Cut Desk: a student's monthly earnings report
dse.cut_report.help: Enter what a student earned in a month (0 is a valid report), the platform fees if their agreement is net, and where the proof is kept. It works out your cut and makes the invoice in the company name as a print-ready page. A big drop against their own recent average gets a friendly prompt, never an accusation. Nothing is sent. The agreement text is a starting point, not legal advice.

fields.name: fees
fields.label: Platform fees they paid (net agreements only)

fields.name: proof
fields.label: Where the proof is (for example: Nov statement in the proofs folder)

fields.name: replace
fields.label: Correct a month already reported (only before anything is paid on it)

dse.cut_paid.label: Cut Desk: a student's cut arrived
dse.cut_paid.help: Records what actually arrived for a cut invoice (leave the amount empty for the whole amount) and adds it to the Cash Desk. If it came in short, usually a transfer fee, it says so; tick Write off the shortfall to accept it.

fields.name: amount
fields.label: Amount that arrived (empty = the whole amount owed)

dse.cut_list.label: Cut Desk: who owes what
dse.cut_list.help: Every student with the cut invoiced, received and owed, and what each one needs (a missing report, an overdue invoice).

dse.cut_show.label: Cut Desk: one student in full
dse.cut_show.help: Every month reported, the cut, the invoice and whether it is settled, with any month that has no proof noted.

dse.cut_status.label: Cut Desk: pause or end an agreement
dse.cut_status.help: Paused or ended students are no longer chased for reports. Unpaid invoices stay payable.

dse.cut_sync.label: Cut Desk: pull students' DFY months from Citadel
dse.cut_sync.help: Students already file their monthly net income in Citadel. This brings every filed month into the Cut Desk as a statement and an invoice (DFY: 20% of net income, capped at $18,000, ending at 12 qualified months), recorded as paid when Citadel already shows it paid. Choose Turn on to let the runner do it every ten minutes. Needs your runner to be an admin's and the DFY bridge SQL run in Supabase. Nothing is sent.

dse.cut_accounts.label: Cut Desk: where students pay (check or publish)
dse.cut_accounts.help: Checks engines/<engine>/payout-accounts.json (Grey, Payoneer or bank accounts) and shows what students currently see on the payment page. Tick Publish to replace what students see. Placeholders in [brackets] are refused so an unfinished list never goes live. This changes what students see, so only publish when the details are right.

fields.name: example
fields.label: Start from the example file (copies it if none exists)

dse.match.label: Statement Matcher: match money received to invoices
dse.match.help: Reads the CSV you exported from Grey, Payoneer or your bank (saved in the engine's statements folder on your PC) and matches the money that came IN to your open invoices: student cuts and client invoices. It uses the invoice number in the reference, the amount (exact, or short by a normal transfer fee), the sender's name and the date. SURE matches (the invoice number and the amount both fit, nothing else fits as well) can be recorded in one go if you tick Record the SURE matches: that does exactly what Paid does, including the Cash Desk and, for DFY months, Citadel. Everything else (likely, more than one fit, no fit) is only shown, with the command to run if you agree. A credit is never applied twice and a different currency is never matched. Nothing is sent.

fields.name: monthfirst
fields.label: Read dates like 03/04/2026 as March 4 (default: day first)

fields.name: tolerance
fields.label: Transfer fee a payment may be short by (empty = 2% of the invoice, $1 to $20)

dse.success.label: Student Success Desk: who needs a check-in, and expected DFY income
dse.success.help: For your DFY students (the filings that Pull students' DFY months brought in). Shows each student's progress (qualified months out of 12, amount remitted out of the $18,000 cap) and flags who needs a check-in, with the facts behind every flag: has not filed, never filed, filed 0 repeatedly, under the $2,000 line (shown as an opportunity when close), a sharp drop against their own average, few qualified months, a remittance overdue, or nearly through. Each flag comes with a short, kind draft message in your name for you to send yourself. The forecast shows your expected DFY income for the coming months from each student's own last three filed months (likely and low), stopping at the cap or 12 qualified months, and leaving out students with too little history. It is a projection, not a promise. Nothing is sent.

choices.label: Overview (progress, flags, the top draft, forecast)

dse.books.label: Books Desk: the monthly pack for your accountant
dse.books.help: Writes a month's records in one place: what you received (cash basis), what you invoiced (accrual basis), what is still owed with ageing, what you wrote off, the exchange rates used, the year to date, and a list of things to check, plus CSV files your accountant can open. Every currency stays in its own currency; money in a currency you gave no exchange rate for is listed as NOT converted, never guessed. It does not work out tax and lists the questions for your accountant. Nothing is sent.

fields.name: month
fields.label: Month (YYYY-MM, empty = the last complete month)

fields.name: base
fields.label: Add everything up in
fields.hint: A 3-letter currency code: USD, GBP, EUR, NGN, CAD, AUD, ZAR, GHS, INR...

dse.fx_add.label: Exchange rates: enter one
dse.fx_add.help: Money in other currencies counts toward your dollar target and your books only at exchange rates YOU enter (the rate your bank, Grey or Payoneer gave you when the money landed, or the one your accountant tells you to use). Nothing is looked up. The most recent rate on or before a payment's date is used.

fields.name: from_cur
fields.label: From (the money you received)
fields.hint: A 3-letter currency code: USD, GBP, EUR, NGN, CAD, AUD, ZAR, GHS, INR...

fields.name: to_cur
fields.label: To
fields.hint: A 3-letter currency code: USD, GBP, EUR, NGN, CAD, AUD, ZAR, GHS, INR...

fields.name: rate
fields.label: How many of the TO currency 1 of the FROM currency buys (like 1.27)

dse.fx_list.label: Exchange rates: the ones I entered
dse.fx_list.help: Every exchange rate you entered for this engine, oldest first.

dse.proof_due.label: Proof Desk: who to ask, follow up or thank
dse.proof_due.help: Shows who is at a good moment to ask for a testimonial and a referral (a client whose work is delivered, a DFY student at 6 and at 12 qualified months), who needs one gentle follow-up, and which referrals have not been thanked, each with the command to run. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_ask.label: Proof Desk: draft a testimonial or referral request
dse.proof_ask.help: Writes a kind, optional request in your name: three easy questions for a testimonial and a referral ask, with how they would like their name shown and whether numbers may be used. A DFY student's request says it is separate from their DFY and that no changes nothing. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_mark.label: Proof Desk: mark an ask sent, answered, declined or closed
dse.proof_mark.help: Keeps the record straight so the desk knows who still needs a follow-up. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_quote.label: Proof Desk: record what someone said, and what they agreed to
dse.proof_quote.help: Keeps their EXACT words and exactly what they agreed to: that you may use the text, how their name is shown (full, first or anonymous), whether the company and any numbers may be shown, and where (proposals, website, social, outreach). Without recorded consent the quote cannot be used anywhere, and you get the message to send them showing exactly how it would appear. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

fields.name: channel
fields.label: Where you got it (for your records)

fields.name: ask
fields.label: The ask it answers (optional, like ASK-001)

fields.name: consent
fields.label: They agreed to my using it

fields.name: consent_how
fields.label: How they agreed (for example: replied yes on WhatsApp, 15 Nov)

fields.name: company
fields.label: May their role and business be shown

fields.name: numbers
fields.label: May numbers they mention be used

fields.name: scope
fields.label: Where it may be used (comma list: proposals,website,social,outreach)

dse.proof_quotes.label: Proof Desk: the quotes I may use
dse.proof_quotes.help: Only approved, consented and not-withdrawn quotes, word for word, with the attribution THEY chose, and only the numbers that are in their own words or match your records. Everything else is listed with the reason it cannot be used. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_withdraw.label: Proof Desk: someone withdrew their quote
dse.proof_withdraw.help: Takes effect at once: the quote is never usable again, and Outreach Preflight blocks any message that still contains it. Remove it from anything already published or sent. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_refer.label: Proof Desk: record a referral
dse.proof_refer.help: Records who introduced whom, so you can write to them this week, mention who suggested you, and thank the referrer (a thank-you draft is shown). Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_thanked.label: Proof Desk: I thanked the referrer
dse.proof_thanked.help: Takes the referral off the thank-you list. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.proof_list.label: Proof Desk: everything at a glance
dse.proof_list.help: Every ask, quote (usable or not, and why) and referral for this engine. Nothing is sent: you send every message yourself.

dse.call_prep.label: Call Desk: prepare for a booked call
dse.call_prep.help: A one-page brief for a booked call, built only from your own records: what you sent, what they wrote in their own words, what their website check or enrichment found (each fact says where it came from), three facts to open with, a question plan under the five scorecard headings with their gap woven in, your up-front contract script, and what must be in hand before you speak. What is not known is listed as not known. Also creates a notes sheet. Nothing is sent.

fields.name: source
fields.label: List the lead is on (like 2026-11-09, see the Send Desk)

dse.call_after.label: Call Desk: what to do the minute the call ends
dse.call_after.help: Type what you heard (their problem in their words, the monthly cost they gave, the price, what you agreed) and get the recap message to send within 10 minutes, the scorecard command, and for a follow-up call the proposal command already filled in. A sold or lost call is written into your send log so your results stay true. Tick Stop to put them on your do-not-contact list if they asked not to be contacted. Nothing is sent.

fields.name: source
fields.label: List the lead is on (like 2026-11-09, see the Send Desk)

fields.name: cost_month
fields.label: What they said it costs them each month ($, 0 if not said)

fields.name: price
fields.label: The price you agreed or will quote ($, 0 if not yet)

fields.name: agreed
fields.label: What you agreed as the next step

fields.name: stop
fields.label: They asked not to be contacted again

dse.brief.label: Daily Brief: what to do first today
dse.brief.help: The few things to do first today across all your engines, in the Weekly Review's fixed order (closest to money first), each with the tool that does it. Your PC builds this by itself in the background and shows it on your Dashboard; run it here to refresh it now. Nothing is sent or changed.

dse.voices_ask.label: Voices: ask the library
dse.voices_ask.help: Type a question or a topic and get the passages that answer it best, each with who said it and where (the book and section, or the Wikiquote source). Choose one figure, or an area, or a path, or everyone. Real words with real sources found by matching your own: no AI model writes or changes them, and nothing is made up. If a figure has not been fetched yet it says so. Nothing is sent.

dse.voices_today.label: Voices: a passage for today
dse.voices_today.help: One passage for today from the library, chosen by the date and the area you pick, with its source. The same passage all day, a different one tomorrow. No AI model.

dse.voices_list.label: Voices: the roster
dse.voices_list.help: The figures in the library: 10 for each area (wisdom, empowerment, structure, sales, financial) and 7 for each path, with what each is known for and how many of their sources are checked and fetched. Filter by area or path.

dse.voices_show.label: Voices: one figure
dse.voices_show.help: Who they are, what they are known for, each source and whether it has been checked, how much of their library is fetched, your own notes, and the latest from their own feeds. Social profiles are shown as links only.

dse.voices_verify.label: Voices: check a figure's sources
dse.voices_verify.help: Checks each source for a figure live (the book is on Project Gutenberg, the Wikiquote page exists, the feed answers, the books are real) and records the result. Nothing is fetched or used until its source is checked here. A failed source can be fixed in the roster and checked again.

dse.voices_fetch.label: Voices: fetch a figure's library
dse.voices_fetch.help: Downloads and indexes the figure's checked public-domain books (Project Gutenberg) and sourced quotations (Wikiquote, CC BY-SA), so Ask can find them. Books still in copyright are not copied: only their titles are listed. Run Check sources first.

dse.voices_update.label: Voices: what is new from the living
dse.voices_update.help: For living figures with a checked feed (their blog or newsletter, their official YouTube channel, their podcast): lists what they have published since the last time, with the date, the link and a short description. You follow the link to read or watch it. Leave the figure on Everyone to check them all. Social networks are never fetched.

dse.voices_note.label: Voices: add your own note
dse.voices_note.help: Add a line you read or heard (from a book in copyright, a talk, a video) to a figure's library, with where it comes from. It is marked as your note wherever it appears, never as their words, and a note without a source is not kept.

fields.name: text
fields.label: The line or idea (8 to 1,200 characters)

fields.name: source
fields.label: Where from (book and page, video and time, talk and date)

dse.voices_setup.label: Voices: set up the library
dse.voices_setup.help: Makes the library work with one click. For every figure it checks each source, repairs what can be repaired (another feed address, the right Project Gutenberg book, a simpler book title), downloads the public-domain texts and sourced quotations, and reads what the living have published. It can be run again and again: it skips what is up to date and carries on where it stopped. It tells you plainly what it could not fix and what to do. Only lawful public sources are used; no social network is read.

dse.mypack.label: Make my own website check (for any business)
dse.mypack.help: The built-in checks are written for one path each. Make your own for any business you sell to. Name it, say in one sentence what you offer, then write up to 4 checks, each as: words that count as the website having it, separated by commas, then =>, then what you would say if none of them appear (the gap you would open with). Example: online booking, book now, schedule => there is no way to book a session online. Your check then appears in the 'Your path or your own check' list of the lead and website tools. Nothing is sent.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name (the kind of business, like Wedding photographers)

fields.name: sells
fields.label: What you offer, in one sentence

fields.name: check1
fields.label: Check 1: words that count as 'has it', then =>, then what you would say if missing
fields.placeholder: online booking, book now, schedule => there is no way to book online

fields.name: check2
fields.label: Check 2: words that count as 'has it', then =>, then what you would say if missing (optional)
fields.placeholder: online booking, book now, schedule => there is no way to book online

fields.name: check3
fields.label: Check 3: words that count as 'has it', then =>, then what you would say if missing (optional)
fields.placeholder: online booking, book now, schedule => there is no way to book online

fields.name: check4
fields.label: Check 4: words that count as 'has it', then =>, then what you would say if missing (optional)
fields.placeholder: online booking, book now, schedule => there is no way to book online

fields.name: pages
fields.label: Pages to look at besides the home page (optional: contact, pricing, booking)

dse.categories.label: Business types: find the exact name for the lead finder
dse.categories.help: Search Foursquare's list of business categories (the data behind the lead finder) for the exact name of the business you sell to, like photographer or yoga studio. You can also just type your own business type in the lead tools: it is found and saved for you.

dse.crm.label: CRM sync: keep this engine's leads, replies and calls in my BPS CRM
dse.crm.help: Your engine already knows every lead, who replied (and what they said), who booked a call and who became a client. This puts them in your BPS CRM so you stop copying: one lead per business, the right stage, and a block in the notes that keeps itself up to date. It is OFF until you turn it on for an engine. Preview shows exactly what the CRM would get. A stage only moves forward, what you wrote in the CRM is never overwritten, and a lead you added yourself is matched by its website and adopted, not duplicated. Nothing is sent to anyone but your own account.

choices.label: Preview what the CRM would get
Send now (it also runs by itself every 5 minutes when on)

periodic.what: My engines: settings from Citadel onto this PC, progress back
Send Desk: your engines' lists on your phone, your phone taps into your log
Monthly goals: a suggested goal for the month ahead, written for you to accept (it never changes a goal)
DFY: students' filed months from Citadel into the Cut Desk (only when you turned it on)
Daily Brief: what to do first today, sent to your Dashboard (nothing is sent to anyone else)
Voices: keeps the thinkers library filled and current (public sources only, no social network)
CRM: the leads, replies and calls of engines you turned on, kept in your BPS CRM (only your own account)
